raw_response:
I am 65 years old and have farmed my 8 mu in Quzhou for over forty years. My middle-school education lets me read pesticide labels and figure fertilizer rates, but I do not experiment at my age. This year I will keep 6.5 mu in winter wheat and summer maize, our backbone rotation. I sow improved wheat in October, rotary till beforehand, spread compound fertilizer as basal, and topdress nitrogen in spring when the wheat greens up; I irrigate four times from my well and spray three times for weeds and insects. After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize with no-tillage straight into the stubble, apply compound fertilizer at sowing, irrigate twice, and spray three times. The remaining 1.5 mu I plant to hybrid cotton for cash. Cotton is labor-intensive—pruning and many sprays—but the income helps. I rotary till the cotton plot, apply basal and topdressed fertilizer, irrigate three times, and spray about ten times for bollworm and weeds. I target roughly 1000 kg per mu for wheat, 1100 kg per mu for maize, and 500 kg per mu for seed cotton.
